what: Target is a US general merchandise retailer with about 1,950 large stores. It sells clothing, home goods, beauty products and groceries, with a focus on its own brands and on same-day fulfilment from stores.
customers: US households, mainly suburban shoppers, in store and through its app and same-day services.
money: apparel, home, beauty, toys and electronics
groceries, household items and pet supplies
moat: Store locations within quick reach of most US consumers that double as fulfilment centres, plus own brands that cannot be price-compared elsewhere.
risks: Sales have fallen for three years as discretionary spending weakened
Walmart has taken share among higher-income shoppers
Theft and shrink have raised costs
Operating margin near 5% leaves little room for error
opportunities: Same-day delivery and drive-up pickup grow faster than store sales and use existing assets
Its retail media advertising business earns high margins on existing traffic
A recovery in discretionary spending would lift margins quickly from a low base
watch: Comparable sales, especially in discretionary categories, and operating margin.
